title: Luke Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 22.

questions.question: In Luke 22, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh
Judas communed with the chief priests
The twelve apostles sat with Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Luke 22:1.

questions.question: Who sought how they might kill Jesus?
questions.explanation: The chief priests and scribes are identified as those who sought how to kill Jesus in Luke 22:2.

questions.question: Who entered into Judas Iscariot?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:3 states that Satan entered into Judas, who was one of the twelve apostles.

questions.question: What did Judas Iscariot agree to give the chief priests?
questions.explanation: The chief priests were glad and covenanted to give Judas money for his betrayal in Luke 22:5.

questions.question: What did Jesus ask Peter and John to prepare?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:8, Jesus specifically asks Peter and John to prepare the Passover.

questions.question: What did Jesus say would happen when they entered the city?
options: They would find a man with a pitcher of water
They would meet the chief priests
They would find a place to eat
questions.correctAnswer: They would find a man with a pitcher of water
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed Peter and John that they would meet a man bearing a pitcher of water in Luke 22:10.

questions.question: What did the goodman of the house show Peter and John?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:12, the goodman shows them a large upper room that is furnished.

questions.question: When did Jesus sit down with the twelve apostles?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:14 states that Jesus sat down with the twelve apostles when the hour had come.

questions.question: What did Jesus express a desire to do before he suffered?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:15, Jesus expresses his desire to eat the Passover with his disciples before he suffers.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the cup he took?
options: It is the new testament in my blood
It is a symbol of suffering
questions.correctAnswer: It is the new testament in my blood
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:20, Jesus says that the cup is the new testament in his blood, which is shed for them.

questions.question: What were the disciples discussing among themselves?
questions.explanation: The disciples began to inquire among themselves who it was that would betray Jesus, as stated in Luke 22:23.

questions.question: There was a strife among the disciples about who should be accounted the greatest.
questions.explanation: Luke 22:24 mentions that there was a strife among them regarding who should be the greatest.

questions.question: The Passover must be killed on the day of unleavened bread.
questions.explanation: According to Luke 22:7, the day of unleavened bread is when the Passover must be killed.

questions.question: Judas Iscariot was the only disciple mentioned in Luke 22.
questions.explanation: Luke 22 mentions that Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve, indicating there were more disciples present.

questions.question: Jesus drank of the fruit of the vine before the kingdom of God shall come.
questions.explanation: Luke 22:18 states that Jesus will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God shall come.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the authority of the kings of the Gentiles?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Luke 22:25, where Jesus explains that kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over the people.

questions.question: What does Luke 22:28 promise will happen if someone serves others as Jesus commanded in Luke 22:26?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:29, Jesus appoints a kingdom to those who serve, as he has received from the Father.

questions.question: Who is said to be among the disciples as one that serves?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:27 states that Jesus is among them as he that serveth, highlighting his role as a servant leader.

questions.question: What does Luke 22:32 say Jesus prayed for concerning Simon Peter?
options: That he would not betray him
That he would lead the others
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:32, Jesus explicitly states that he prayed for Peter's faith to not fail, emphasizing the importance of faith.

questions.question: What did Jesus instruct his disciples to do in Luke 22:40?
options: Pray that they enter not into temptation
questions.correctAnswer: Pray that they enter not into temptation
questions.explanation: Luke 22:40 shows Jesus instructing his disciples to pray to avoid temptation, highlighting the vital role of prayer in spiritual strength.

questions.question: In Luke 22:42, what does Jesus ask the Father to remove from him?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:42, Jesus asks the Father if it is possible to remove this cup, indicating his desire for relief from the impending suffering.

questions.question: What did Jesus find his disciples doing when he returned from prayer in Luke 22:45?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:45 indicates that when Jesus returned, he found his disciples sleeping due to sorrow, illustrating their struggle at that moment.

questions.question: What was Jesus’s response to Judas when he approached to betray him with a kiss?
options: Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?
questions.correctAnswer: Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:48, Jesus confronts Judas about his betrayal, highlighting the gravity of the act in the moment of betrayal.

questions.question: What did Jesus say would happen before Peter denied him thrice?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:34, Jesus foretells that Peter will deny him three times before the rooster crows, emphasizing Peter's impending failure.

questions.question: According to Jesus in Luke 22:36, what should someone do if they do not have a sword?
options: Sell their garment to buy one
questions.correctAnswer: Sell their garment to buy one
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:36, Jesus instructs his disciples to sell their garment if they do not have a sword, indicating the seriousness of the coming events.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the disciples' experience when he sent them out without provisions in Luke 22:35?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:35, the disciples affirmed that they lacked nothing when sent out without provisions, highlighting their reliance on God.

questions.question: What does Luke 22:24 reveal about the disciples during the Last Supper?
options: They were arguing about who was the greatest
questions.correctAnswer: They were arguing about who was the greatest
questions.explanation: Luke 22:24 reveals that there was a strife among the disciples about who should be considered the greatest, highlighting their human nature.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus prayed earnestly in anguish, as described in Luke 22:44?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:44 states that Jesus prayed more earnestly and was in agony, indicating the depth of his struggle in prayer.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus did not want to suffer and prayed for it to be lifted from him?
questions.explanation: While Jesus asked for the cup to be removed, he ultimately submitted to the Father's will, as seen in Luke 22:42.

questions.question: Is it true that the disciples were fully awake and attentive during Jesus's prayer?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:45 shows that the disciples were sleeping, indicating their lack of alertness during a critical time.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 22.

questions.question: In Luke 22:49, what did those who were about Jesus ask him when they saw what would follow?
options: Lord, shall we smite with the sword?
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, shall we smite with the sword?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:49 shows that those around Jesus asked, 'Lord, shall we smite with the sword?' when they saw the approaching danger.

questions.question: According to Luke 22:50, who was struck and what was the result?
options: The servant of the high priest was struck and his right ear was cut off.
Peter was struck and his hand was wounded.
A disciple was struck and his left ear was cut off.
Jesus was struck and his robe was torn.
questions.correctAnswer: The servant of the high priest was struck and his right ear was cut off.
questions.explanation: Luke 22:50 states that one of Jesus' followers struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.

questions.question: What action did Jesus take after the servant's ear was cut off in Luke 22:51?
options: He touched the ear and healed him.
questions.correctAnswer: He touched the ear and healed him.
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:51, Jesus said, 'Suffer ye thus far,' and then touched the servant's ear and healed him.

questions.question: In Luke 22:52, how does Jesus rebuke the chief priests, captains of the temple, and elders who came to arrest him?
options: Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?
Are ye come with peace to learn from me?
Why do you seek to kill me?
Do you not know I am the Son of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:52 records Jesus asking them if they have come out as against a thief with swords and staves, rebuking their violent approach.

questions.question: What does Jesus say in Luke 22:53 about his time daily with the temple leaders compared to this moment?
options: When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
I have taught openly in the temple, yet you have listened.
You have always welcomed me in the temple.
This is the hour of light, not darkness.
questions.correctAnswer: When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
questions.explanation: Luke 22:53 contrasts Jesus' peaceful daily presence in the temple with the violent arrest, calling it the hour of darkness and power of darkness.

questions.question: In Luke 22:54, who followed Jesus after his arrest and at what distance?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:54 specifically states that Peter followed Jesus afar off after Jesus was taken away.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'kagchoreo' in Luke 22:51 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word translated as 'Suffer' in Luke 22:51 (Greek: 'kagchoreo') means 'to suffer' or 'to allow,' indicating Jesus permitted the action to a point.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Luke 22:49-53 to contrast Jesus' arrest with his previous time in the temple?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:49-53 uses irony by highlighting that Jesus, who was peaceful in the temple, is arrested violently as if a thief, emphasizing the injustice.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Jesus' statement in Luke 22:37 about being 'reckoned among the transgressors'?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:37 quotes Isaiah 53:12, where the suffering servant is 'reckoned with the transgressors,' connecting Jesus' passion with Messianic prophecy.

questions.question: The denial of Peter in Luke 22:56-62 parallels which Old Testament figure's failure under pressure?
questions.explanation: Peter's denial under pressure in Luke 22 echoes King David's failures and repentance, showing human weakness and need for forgiveness (cf. 2 Samuel 11-12).

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Peter denying Jesus the first time in Luke 22?
options: Peter sitting among those who kindled a fire in the hall.
Judas betraying Jesus with a kiss.
Jesus praying on the Mount of Olives.
questions.correctAnswer: Peter sitting among those who kindled a fire in the hall.
questions.explanation: Luke 22:55 states that Peter sat among those who had kindled a fire in the hall, which precedes the maid's identification and Peter's denial in verse 56.

questions.question: Which literary technique is evident in Jesus' repeated use of 'Before the cock crow' in Luke 22:34 and 22:61?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Before the cock crow' in Luke 22:34 and 22:61 forms an inclusio, framing Peter's denial within a literary bracket.

questions.question: How does Luke 22:31-32 illustrate typology in the relationship between Jesus and Peter?
options: Jesus as the intercessor praying for Peter who will fall but be restored.
Peter as a priest offering sacrifices.
Jesus as a warrior fighting Satan.
Peter as a king ruling Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus as the intercessor praying for Peter who will fall but be restored.
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:31-32, Jesus intercedes for Peter's faith not to fail, foreshadowing Peter's denial and later restoration, typifying intercessory prayer.

questions.question: Which Old Testament theme is fulfilled by Jesus' statement in Luke 22:69 about sitting at the right hand of God?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:69 echoes Psalm 110:1, where the Messiah sits at God's right hand, asserting divine authority and kingship.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 22:49, the disciples immediately used swords to defend Jesus at his arrest.
questions.explanation: Luke 22:49 records that the disciples asked Jesus if they should use swords, but it was one disciple who struck, not an immediate collective action.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 22:20 teach about salvation?
options: The new covenant is established through Jesus' blood
Salvation is only for the Jewish people
questions.correctAnswer: The new covenant is established through Jesus' blood
questions.explanation: Luke 22:20 states, 'This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you,' teaching that salvation is secured by Jesus' sacrificial blood in the new covenant.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 22:31 teach about spiritual warfare and divine providence?
options: Satan desires to test believers but God intercedes for them
Satan has no power over believers
God causes believers to sin for His purposes
questions.correctAnswer: Satan desires to test believers but God intercedes for them
questions.explanation: Luke 22:31 says, 'Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat,' indicating spiritual testing, and verse 32 shows Jesus praying for Peter’s faith, illustrating divine intercession.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 22:29-30 teach about the eschatological role of the apostles?
options: The apostles are appointed to reign and judge in God's kingdom
The apostles will lead a political revolution
The apostles lose their authority after Jesus' death
The apostles only have a symbolic role in the church
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles are appointed to reign and judge in God's kingdom
questions.explanation: Luke 22:29-30 states Jesus appoints the apostles a kingdom to eat and drink at His table and sit on thrones judging Israel’s tribes, signifying their eschatological authority.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 22:42 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Luke 22:42, Jesus prays, 'nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done,' demonstrating His submissive obedience to God's sovereign will.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 22:43 demonstrate through the angel's appearance?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:43 records an angel strengthening Jesus, showing God's attribute of providing supernatural strength in times of trial.

questions.question: How does Luke 22:19-20 connect to the broader biblical theme of covenant renewal?
options: It institutes the new covenant through Jesus' body and blood
It emphasizes animal sacrifice as central
It focuses solely on Old Testament law
questions.correctAnswer: It institutes the new covenant through Jesus' body and blood
questions.explanation: These verses recount Jesus offering bread and wine as His body and blood, fulfilling Jeremiah’s prophecy of a new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31) and continuing God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: In what way does Luke 22:34-62 prepare for Christ's passion in the narrative of the Gospels?
options: It foreshadows Peter’s denial and highlights human weakness
It shows Jesus conquering His enemies without suffering
It minimizes the significance of the crucifixion
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Peter’s denial and highlights human weakness
questions.explanation: These verses predict Peter’s denial and portray Jesus’ arrest and mockery, preparing readers for the passion by emphasizing disciples’ frailty and Jesus' willing submission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 22:19 and Luke 22:20 teach about the Lord's Supper?
options: It is a memorial of Christ’s body given and blood shed establishing the new covenant
It is merely a cultural tradition without spiritual meaning
It is a symbol of Old Testament sacrifices only
It grants automatic salvation by participation
questions.correctAnswer: It is a memorial of Christ’s body given and blood shed establishing the new covenant
questions.explanation: Luke 22:19 presents the bread as Christ’s body given for believers, and verse 20 calls the cup the new testament in His blood, together teaching the Lord’s Supper as a memorial and covenant sign.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 22:31 and Luke 22:32 teach about divine intercession and human weakness?
options: God prays for believers so that their faith does not fail despite Satan’s attacks
Believers never face temptation due to divine protection
Human will alone overcomes sin without God’s help
God causes believers to fail as punishment
questions.correctAnswer: God prays for believers so that their faith does not fail despite Satan’s attacks
questions.explanation: Verse 31 warns of Satan’s desire to sift believers, while verse 32 affirms Jesus’ prayer for Peter’s faith to endure and to strengthen others, illustrating divine intercession amid human weakness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 22:26 and Luke 22:27 teach about Christian leadership?
options: True greatness in leadership is servant-heartedness modeled by Christ
Authority in the church is based on worldly power and status
Leaders should dominate others to maintain order
Christian leaders are exempt from serving others
questions.correctAnswer: True greatness in leadership is servant-heartedness modeled by Christ
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches in verse 26 to be like the younger and serve, and in verse 27 He exemplifies this by being among them as one who serves, defining Christian leadership as humble service.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Luke 22:36-38 teaches Christians should always be armed and violent. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Jesus instructs His disciples to be prepared for coming trials symbolized by swords
Christians must forsake all weapons and passively suffer
The passage promotes literal warfare as a Christian duty
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus instructs His disciples to be prepared for coming trials symbolized by swords
questions.explanation: Luke 22:36-38 uses swords symbolically to prepare disciples for opposition, not to endorse violence, as shown by Jesus’ rebuke of violent defense in verses 49-51.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 22:53 teach about the spiritual conflict surrounding Jesus' arrest?
options: This is the hour and power of darkness, indicating cosmic spiritual opposition
Jesus was arrested due to lack of divine protection
Human authorities acted according to God’s pleasure
The arrest was a random human event without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: This is the hour and power of darkness, indicating cosmic spiritual opposition
questions.explanation: Luke 22:53 states 'this is your hour, and the power of darkness,' highlighting that Jesus’ arrest involves spiritual forces opposing God’s plan.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 22:15 teach about Christ's desire in relation to salvation history?
options: Christ earnestly desired to share the Passover before His suffering, emphasizing His willing sacrifice
Christ was reluctant to suffer and tried to avoid it
Christ’s desire was only for earthly kingdom establishment
questions.correctAnswer: Christ earnestly desired to share the Passover before His suffering, emphasizing His willing sacrifice
questions.explanation: Luke 22:15 shows Jesus’ deep longing to eat the Passover with His disciples before suffering, signifying His willing participation in salvation history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 22:47 and Luke 22:48 teach about Judas’ betrayal?
options: Judas’ betrayal is a deliberate act of treachery revealed by Jesus’ awareness
Judas was unaware of his betrayal
The betrayal was accidental and unintentional
questions.correctAnswer: Judas’ betrayal is a deliberate act of treachery revealed by Jesus’ awareness
questions.explanation: Luke 22:47-48 portrays Judas approaching Jesus to betray Him with a kiss, and Jesus confronting him, confirming the intentional nature of Judas’ betrayal.

questions.question: How does Luke 22:25-27 teach about the contrast between worldly and kingdom leadership?
options: Kingdom leadership is servant leadership, unlike worldly lordship
Kingdom leaders exercise lordship and authority like kings
Worldly leadership and kingdom leadership are the same
questions.correctAnswer: Kingdom leadership is servant leadership, unlike worldly lordship
questions.explanation: Jesus contrasts Gentile rulers who lord it over others with His followers who are to serve and be humble, redefining leadership in kingdom terms (Luke 22:25-27).
